# Overview

This vignette goes from the CosMx flat files of a mouse brain section to
an interactive app on the dentate gyrus:

1. read the data and compute per-cell quality metrics on the whole section;
2. flag low-quality cells and look at them in the QC app;
3. keep the nine fields of view (FOVs) around the dentate gyrus, with cell
    polygons and cell types;
4. compute niches and spatial domains;
5. explore everything in the analysis app: FOV selection, polygons,
    spatial statistics, spatially variable genes.

The data are a CosMx 1,000-plex section of mouse brain (Bruker), used in
the [OSTA book](https://lmweber.org/OSTA/) and distributed by
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("OSTA.data")` (about 40 MB, downloaded once and then
cached).

# Reading the data

```{r libraries}
library(spiSEE)
library(SpaceTrooper)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r download, eval = FALSE}
# OSTA.data_load() changes the working directory on first download:
# run it from a temporary one.
zip <- withr::with_dir(tempdir(),
    OSTA.data::OSTA.data_load("CosMx1k_MouseBrain2", mol = FALSE))
```

```{r download-retry, include = FALSE}
# The same call, tried up to three times: the data are hosted on OSF, which
# sometimes refuses downloads from build servers. Without the data, the
# rest of the code is shown but not run.
zip <- NULL
for (i in seq_len(3)) {
    zip <- tryCatch(withr::with_dir(tempdir(),
        OSTA.data::OSTA.data_load("CosMx1k_MouseBrain2", mol = FALSE)),
        error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(zip)) break
    Sys.sleep(60 * i)
}
have_data <- !is.null(zip)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = have_data)
```

`r if (!have_data) paste("**Note:** the data could not be downloaded when",
"this vignette was built, so the code below is shown without its output.")`

```{r unzip}
dir <- tempfile()
unzip(zip, exdir = dir)
list.files(dir)
```

`readCosmxSPE()` from `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("SpaceTrooper")` reads the
counts, the cell metadata and the FOV positions into a
`SpatialExperiment`:

```{r read}
spe <- readCosmxSPE(dirName = dir, sampleName = "MouseBrain")
spe
length(unique(spe$fov))
```

# Quality control of the whole section

`spatialPerCellQC()` adds per-cell metrics: total counts, detected genes,
cell area in µm², aspect ratio, distance to the FOV border, and the ratio
of negative-control counts. Cells with no counts are removed.

```{r qc}
spe <- spatialPerCellQC(spe)
summary(spe$Area_um)
```

The metrics are combined into one quality score per cell, `QScore`,
between 0 and 1. Outliers of a single metric are flagged with
medcouple-adjusted fences (robust to skewed distributions), here for the
total counts, which the score does not use, and for the cell area.

```{r qscore}
set.seed(1998)   # the score's model is trained on a random sample of cells
spe <- computeQScore(spe)
spe <- computeQScoreFlags(spe, qsThreshold = 0.5)
table(low_QScore = spe$low_QScore)
spe <- computeSpatialOutlier(spe, computeBy = "total", method = "mc")
spe <- computeSpatialOutlier(spe, computeBy = "Area_um", method = "mc")
```

The cell polygons are read once the score is computed:

```{r polygons-read}
spe <- readAndAddPolygonsToSPE(spe)
```

```{r qc-hist, dev = "svglite", crop = NULL, fig.height = 3.5}
#| fig.cap = "Total counts per cell with the outlier fences."
plotMetricHist(spe, metric = "total", useFences = "total_outlier_mc")
```

`plotSpatialCells()` draws the cells as their polygons, coloured by any
annotation, QC metric or gene, as in the app:

```{r qc-map, fig.height = 6.5}
#| fig.cap = paste("Quality score of every cell of the section, on the",
#|     "cell polygons.")
plotSpatialCells(spe, "QScore")
```

The section has 130 FOVs. The dentate gyrus lies in nine of them (3 × 3):

```{r fov-map, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 9}
#| fig.cap = "FOV layout (left) and the nine dentate gyrus FOVs (right)."
dg_fovs <- c(98:100, 113:115, 122:124)
plotZoomFovsMap(spe, fovs = dg_fovs, colourBy = "QScore")
```

## The QC app

The QC app shows the same metrics interactively. Each FOV is a tile on the
overview map: clicking tiles (or dragging a box over several) and pressing
*Validate* restricts every other panel to them; *Clear* goes back to the
whole section. A selection can also be given at launch with `selection =`,
as here for the nine dentate gyrus FOVs. The QC histograms count the cells
outside the outlier fences in the selection, the FOV zoom panel shows
where the selected FOVs lie and their cells coloured by the quality score,
and the last panel compares the QC metrics of the selected FOVs.

```{r app-qc}
spe <- setPlatform(spe, "cosmx")
app <- spiSEE(spe, mode = "qc", cache = FALSE,
                    selection = paste(dg_fovs, collapse = ","))
if (interactive()) shiny::runApp(app)
```

```{r shot-qc, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
#| fig.cap = paste("QC app on the whole section with the nine dentate",
#|     "gyrus FOVs selected (orange): total counts, QC histograms with outlier",
#|     "fences, the FOV zoom coloured by quality score and the QC metrics",
#|     "per FOV.")
knitr::include_graphics("figures/cosmx_qc.jpg")
```

Low-quality cells (dark in the FOV zoom) concentrate at FOV borders and
along a few tissue edges, which is easier to see on the map than in a
table.

# The dentate gyrus

We keep the nine FOVs and the cells that pass QC.

```{r subset}
dg <- spe[, spe$fov %in% dg_fovs & !spe$low_QScore]
dg
```

## Cell types

The annotation distributed with the data gives one cell type per cell;
the few unannotated cells are removed.

```{r labels}
ann <- read.csv(file.path(dir, "annotation.csv"))
key <- match(paste(dg$fov, dg$cellID), paste(ann$fov, ann$cell_ID))
dg$cell_type <- ann$Annotation[key]
dg <- dg[, !is.na(dg$cell_type)]
dg$cell_type <- factor(dg$cell_type)
head(sort(table(dg$cell_type), decreasing = TRUE), 12)
```

For the static figures, the twelve most frequent types are kept and the
rest grouped as "other":

```{r top-types}
top <- names(sort(table(dg$cell_type), decreasing = TRUE))[1:12]
dg$cell_type_top <- factor(ifelse(dg$cell_type %in% top,
                                    as.character(dg$cell_type), "other"),
                            levels = c(top, "other"))
pal <- c(setNames(unname(pals::glasbey(12)), top), other = "grey85")
```

The polygons show the granule cell layer of the dentate gyrus, the CA
fields of the hippocampus, the habenula and the choroid plexus:

```{r polygons, fig.height = 7, fig.width = 9}
#| fig.cap = "Cell polygons coloured by cell type."
plotSpatialCells(dg, "cell_type_top", palette = pal)
```

One FOV in detail, with cell borders:

```{r polygons-fov, dev = "svglite", crop = NULL, fig.height = 6}
#| fig.cap = "FOV 99, cell borders drawn."
plotSpatialCells(dg[, dg$fov == 99], "cell_type_top", palette = pal,
                borders = TRUE) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Normalisation and marker genes

Negative-control probes are removed before normalisation.

```{r norm}
dg <- dg[!grepl("^NegPrb|^Negative|^SystemControl", rownames(dg)), ]
# Library-size normalisation (size factors centred at 1), then log2(x + 1).
cn <- SingleCellExperiment::counts(dg)
sf <- Matrix::colSums(cn)
SingleCellExperiment::logcounts(dg) <- log2(t(t(cn) / (sf / mean(sf))) + 1)
```

Three markers, one per structure: *Adcy1* (granule cells), *Pcp4*
(habenula) and *Ttr* (choroid plexus).

```{r markers, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 10}
#| fig.cap = "Marker genes on the cell polygons (logcounts)."
plotSpatialCells(dg, c("Adcy1", "Pcp4", "Ttr"), ncol = 3)
```

# Niches and spatial domains

The spatial neighbour graph is built once (k nearest cells) and stored on
the object. k sets the scale: a small k describes direct contacts, a large
k a wider region.

```{r graph}
dg <- setPlatform(dg, "cosmx")
dg <- buildSpatialGraph(dg, k = 15)
```

## Niches

A niche groups cells whose neighbourhoods have a similar cell-type
composition. Each niche is named after the two cell types most
over-represented in it compared with the whole region, so a rare type can
appear in a name when it is concentrated in that niche.

```{r niches}
dg <- computeNiches(dg, label_col = "cell_type", k = 15, n_niches = 6)
table(dg$niche)
```

```{r niche-polygons, fig.cap = "Niches.", fig.height = 8, fig.width = 8}
plotSpatialCells(dg, "niche")
```

Each cell's neighbourhood composition is stored as a reduced dimension.
Averaged per niche, it shows what each niche is made of:

```{r niche-heatmap, dev = "svglite", crop = NULL}
#| fig.height = 6, fig.width = 8,
#| fig.cap = paste("Mean neighbourhood composition per niche (twelve most",
#|     "frequent cell types).")
comp <- reducedDim(dg, "NicheComposition")
mean_comp <- apply(comp[, top], 2, function(x) tapply(x, dg$niche, mean))
rownames(mean_comp) <- sub(":.*", "", rownames(mean_comp))
pheatmap::pheatmap(mean_comp, cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
                    angle_col = 315, fontsize_col = 8,
                    color = pals::brewer.blues(50))
```

`niche_entropy` measures how mixed each neighbourhood is (0 = a single
cell type):

```{r entropy, fig.cap = "Neighbourhood entropy.", fig.height = 6}
plotSpatialCells(dg, "niche_entropy")
```

## Spatial domains

Spatial domains cluster expression combined with the neighbourhood average
(`lambda` = weight of the neighbourhood; `lambda = 0` gives plain
expression clusters, also returned as `expr_cluster` for comparison). A
PCA is needed first.

```{r domains}
pca <- prcomp(t(as.matrix(logcounts(dg))), rank. = 20)
reducedDim(dg, "PCA") <- pca$x
dg <- computeSpatialDomains(dg, k_spatial = 15, lambda = 0.2,
                            resolution = 0.5)
table(domain = dg$spatial_domain)
```

```{r domain-plot, fig.height = 4.8, fig.width = 10}
#| fig.cap = "Expression clusters (left) and spatial domains (right)."
plotSpatialCells(dg, c("expr_cluster", "spatial_domain"), ncol = 2) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
```

With `lambda = 0.2` the domains stay close to the expression clusters.
The difference is in mixed areas: at the top right, cells of two
intermixed expression clusters form one domain. A larger `lambda` gives
smoother domains.

The niches and domains are now stored in the object. The app shows them
without recomputing, and recomputes them on a selected region on request.

# The analysis app

```{r app}
app <- spiSEE(dg, mode = "analysis", cache = FALSE)
if (interactive()) shiny::runApp(app)
```

## Selecting a region

Clicking FOV tiles on the overview map, then *Validate*, restricts every
panel to these FOVs: spatial plots zoom in, and statistics, gene rankings
and niches are recomputed on the region when *Compute* is pressed. A
second click on a validated tile removes it; *Clear* returns to the whole
dataset.

The same selection works cell by cell for platforms without fields of
view. For Xenium and Visium HD data (`loadXenium()`, `loadVisiumHD()`),
or any `SpatialExperiment` whose platform is not CosMx, the overview map
shows every cell as a point: clicking adds or removes a cell, and the box
tool selects all the cells in a rectangle, also on sections of more than
100,000 cells. The rest of the app is unchanged.

## Spatial statistics

The statistics panel offers, for a gene or for the cell types:

* the spatial neighbour graph used (k nearest cells);
* global and local Moran's I and the Moran scatter plot
    (`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("Voyager")`);
* local cluster significance (high-high, low-low, ...) at a level set in
    the panel;
* join-count statistics and a cell-type co-occurrence heatmap;
* the L-function of the most frequent cell type and the L-cross function
    of the two most frequent ones (`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("spatialFDA")`).

```{r shot-stats, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
#| fig.cap = paste("Local Moran's I of Adcy1 (left) and cell-type",
#|     "co-occurrence of the twelve most frequent types (right), k = 15.")
knitr::include_graphics("figures/cosmx_stats.jpg")
```

The granule cell layer stands out as two bands of high local Moran's I
for *Adcy1*. The co-occurrence heatmap (join-count z-scores) shows that
each structure is mostly made of one cell type (the strong diagonal), and
which types are neighbours more often than expected, e.g. habenula
inhibitory neurons with thalamic astrocytes. Any categorical column can be
used, here the grouping into twelve types plus "other".

## Spatially variable genes and niches

The SVG panel ranks genes by spatial autocorrelation on the selected
region; clicking a gene shows it in the linked spatial plot. On these FOVs
the top genes mark the structures seen above: *Ttr* (choroid plexus),
*Nrgn*, *Camk2a* and *Adcy1* (neurons, granule cells), *Mbp* (white
matter). The niche
panel switches between niches, their composition, entropy, domains and
expression clusters, drawn on the polygons.

```{r shot-svg, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
#| fig.cap = paste("Spatially variable genes linked to a spatial plot",
#|     "(left) and niches on the polygons (right).")
knitr::include_graphics("figures/cosmx_svg_niches.jpg")
```

## A custom layout

Any combination of panels, including standard iSEE panels, can be opened
with `initial =`. Here: the map, polygons by cell type, the PCA coloured
by niche, and the local Moran's I of *Adcy1* computed at launch (any
non-empty `ComputeTrigger` computes the panel when the app opens):

```{r custom}
panels <- list(
    SpatialMapPanel(),
    SpatialPlotPanel(ColorBy = "cell_type", UsePolygons = TRUE),
    iSEE::ReducedDimensionPlot(Type = "PCA", ColorBy = "Column data",
                                ColorByColumnData = "niche"),
    SpatialStatsPanel(PlotType = "localmoran_plot", Genes = "Adcy1",
                        K = 15L, ComputeTrigger = "launch"))
app <- spiSEE(dg, initial = panels, cache = FALSE)
```

## Saving the prepared object

The object can be saved and reopened directly in the app later
(`loadCosmx()` sets the platform):

```{r save, eval = FALSE}
saveRDS(dg, "dentate_gyrus.rds")
app <- spiSEE(loadCosmx("dentate_gyrus.rds"))
```
